subject.title: [Feature]: Move away from useMultiFileAuthState for Baileys

question: Should the bundled WhatsApp plugin adopt a transactional SQLite authentication store, and which database API, migration, rollback, permissions, and legacy-file cleanup contract should become permanent?
rationale: The evidence proves the production-storage gap, but selecting the long-term sensitive-state owner and compatibility boundary requires maintainer product and security intent.

options.title: Approve transactional SQLite migration
options.body: Define a plugin-owned transactional store, migrate and verify all credential and signal-key categories, preserve a restricted rollback path, and remove legacy files after success.

options.title: Retain hardened multi-file storage
options.body: Continue targeted durability and performance hardening while explicitly accepting Baileys' production warning and the remaining multi-file operational costs.

recommendation.title: Approve transactional SQLite migration
recommendation.body: Define a plugin-owned transactional store, migrate and verify all credential and signal-key categories, preserve a restricted rollback path, and remove legacy files after success.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest recent history on WhatsApp authentication persistence, backup recovery, and its regression tests is tied to this contributor.
